canonical_statement: Let C be a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus at least 2 over a number field K, let J be its Jacobian with a symmetric ample theta divisor, and embed C into J using a degree-one divisor. There is an epsilon > 0 such that the points of C over the algebraic closure of K whose Neron-Tate height is at most epsilon are finite.
domain_and_universes: Number field K; smooth projective geometrically connected curve C/K; genus g >= 2; Jacobian J/K; theta polarization; algebraic points C(Kbar). Exact Lean universes remain open.
quantifiers: C/K : smooth projective geometrically connected curve with genus at least 2
J : Jacobian C and j : C -> J induced by a degree-one divisor
there exists epsilon : Real with 0 < epsilon
hypotheses: K has characteristic zero and is a number field
C is smooth, projective, and geometrically connected
the height is the canonical Neron-Tate height associated to a symmetric theta divisor
conclusion: {x in C(Kbar) | canonicalHeight (j x) <= epsilon} is finite

alternate_encodings.target: The essential minimum of j(C) for the Neron-Tate height is positive
alternate_encodings.relationship: standard equivalent formulation of non-density for a curve
alternate_encodings.checked_witness: none; equivalence must be formalized and checked in a later phase

alternate_encodings.target: Small-height points are not Zariski dense in j(C)
alternate_encodings.relationship: for an irreducible curve, every proper closed subset is finite

excluded_degenerate_cases: Genus zero and one are excluded. The claim is not the later general Bogomolov theorem for arbitrary subvarieties of abelian varieties, and it is not a statement about all algebraic points having positive height.
